Save a figure as a static image

Source: R/chromote.R, R/save_image.R
save_image.Rd

Exports a figure to PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, PDF or EPS with plotly.js's own image export, using the plotly.js bundled with this package in headless Chrome (driven by the chromote package). No Python is needed.

Usage

chrome_exporter(...)

save_image(p, file, ..., width = NULL, height = NULL, scale = NULL)

Arguments

...

Unused.

p

A go_figure() or a plotly htmlwidget (anything as_widget() accepts).

file

Output file; the format is taken from the extension (.png, .jpeg, .jpg, .webp, .svg, .pdf or .eps).

width, height

Image size in pixels. Default: the figure's layout width and height, or 700 x 500.

scale

Multiplier for the image resolution (e.g. 2 for high-DPI PNGs).

Value

save_image() returns file invisibly. chrome_exporter() returns an exporter with transform() and shutdown() functions.

Details

It uses the browser set by the CHROMOTE_CHROME environment variable, an installed Google Chrome, another installed Chromium-based browser (Microsoft Edge, which every Windows 10/11 machine has, Chromium or Brave, also when installed for the current user only), or a Chrome Headless Shell downloaded by chromote. Without any of these, an interactive session asks whether to download Chrome Headless Shell (about 100 MB, kept for later sessions); elsewhere, download it once with chromote::chrome_versions_add("latest-stable", "chrome-headless-shell").

The browser is started on the first export and reused for later ones. Fonts are the ones installed on this computer: save_image() warns when a font a figure asks for is not installed (see available_fonts()).

Large figures can take a while to draw: an export waits up to getOption("plotly.core.export_timeout", 300) seconds. LaTeX (see TeX()) is typeset with the MathJax bundled with the package, so it works offline. PDF is made by printing the SVG image to a page of the figure's size; EPS is converted from the SVG image with the rsvg package.

Downloads

save_image() downloads nothing on its own in scripts, tests or examples. In an interactive session that needs set-up, it asks first (see install_chrome()). What it may download keeps its own licence (see the package's COPYRIGHTS file): Chrome Headless Shell (from Google's Chrome for Testing, kept in chromote's cache), on Linux the shared libraries Chrome needs (your distribution's packages, kept in tools::R_user_dir("plotly.core", "cache")). remove_chrome() removes the downloads.

chrome_exporter() returns an exporter of its own, whose transform(p, file, ...) function writes images; call its shutdown() function when done.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fig <- iris |> go_figure() |> add_scatter(x = ~Sepal.Width, y = ~Sepal.Length, mode = "markers")
save_image(fig, tempfile(fileext = ".png"), width = 800, height = 500, scale = 2)
save_image(fig, tempfile(fileext = ".svg"))
} # }
